english.title: Breach of pre-charge bail condition not to leave the United Kingdom
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having been arrested under section 24 of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 in respect of an offence mentioned in section 41(1) or (2) of the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008, and having been released without charge and on bail under Part 4 of the 1984 Act subject to a travel restriction condition not to leave the United Kingdom, failed to comply with that condition
english.legislation: Contrary to section 68(3)(a) and (4) of the Policing and Crime Act 2017.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
arrested under section 24 PACE
released without charge and on bail under Part 4 of PACE
subject to travel restriction condition not to leave the UK
failed to comply

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) For any travel restriction other than not to leave the UK, refer to the offence in section 68(3)(b), H18820/PC17003.
(ii) Where a person is released without charge and on bail under PACE, the offence is treated as having been committed in England and Wales, whether or not the conduct constituting the offence took place there, see section 68(5) of the Policing and Crime Act 2017.

other.powersofarrest:
Arrest without warrant - PACE
Also consider: arrest without warrant - terrorism
other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Twelve months imprisonment and / or fine.
EITHER WAY: Twelve months imprisonment and / or fine.

Note:
In relation to an offence committed before paragraph 24(2) of Schedule 22 to the Sentencing Act 2020 comes into force (01/12/20), the reference to 12 months imprisonment in relation to summary offences, above, is to be read as a reference to 6 months imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
